correctness.rationale: The classical normalized Poisson-kernel Fourier series has coefficient at mode \(2n\) of modulus \(r\). Its reciprocal integrates exactly to \(C_\mu=4\pi^2(1+r^2)/(1-r^2)\), since the cosine averages to zero. Substitution into the source-stated \(\overline K=12\pi^2n^2/[C_\mu(1-|\widehat\mu(2n)|^2)]\) cancels \(1-r^2\) and yields \(3n^2/(1+r^2)\). The limit is \(3n^2/2>0\) while \(C_\mu\to\infty\). At \(r=0\) the value is \(3n^2\), matching the stated uniform-measure normalization. Thus the calculation rigorously contradicts a universal decay clause under that exact formula; the source premise was not independently verified in full text due to access.

value.rationale: The explicit smooth counterexample identifies a missing factor in a published curvature-limit argument while preserving the principal nonflatness and sharp upper-bound theorems. It delineates an important boundary of geometric degeneration claims using a canonical harmonic family.

final_claim: For each \(n\ge1\), the Poisson-kernel smooth probability densities \(\rho_{r,n}(\theta)=(1-r^2)/(2\pi(1-2r\cos(2n\theta)+r^2))\) with \(0\le r<1\) satisfy \(C_\mu=4\pi^2(1+r^2)/(1-r^2)\) and \(|\widehat\mu(2n)|=r\), so the published equal-frequency Fourier-plane curvature formula gives \(\overline K=3n^2/(1+r^2)\to3n^2/2\) while \(C_\mu\to\infty\). This refutes an unrestricted curvature-decay assertion attributed to Corollary 3.12 of arXiv:2610.00625, not its curvature formula or upper bound.
limitations: All measures used in the argument have \(r<1\); the singular limiting measure is not claimed to lie in the smooth manifold.
